display.title: Trust the Rebbe's Words
display.summary_short: An evicted innkeeper fears the Tzemach Tzedek sent his letter to the wrong Moshe, until a poritz's broken wagon stops outside that very house.
display.summary_long: Reb Yankel, an innkeeper near the town of Kamen in the Vitebsk region, is thrown out of his inn by the poritz after a hard year. The Tzemach Tzedek tells him to trust in Hashem and gives him a letter for his Chassid Moshe Ratner, asking him to speak to the poritz. But there are two men named Moshe in Kamen. Moshe the short one inherited wealth and connections with the poritzim from his father Shimshon, whom the town loved so much that Nachum the melamed once tried to take his place at the gallows when Polish rebels wanted to hang him. Moshe Ratner, the tall one, is only a kind storekeeper. The Rebbe's sons assure Yankel that their father does not make mistakes. That night, as Yankel says Tehillim in Moshe Ratner's attic, a poritz's wagon breaks down outside, drawn by the only light in the street. Moshe welcomes him, refuses payment for his hospitality, and asks only that his friend be given back his inn. The poritz signs the inn over to Yankel for good. The storyteller ends with the Rebbe's words that the time of the Geulah has come.
display.lesson: A Rebbe's words come true exactly as he says them; trust them and trust in Hashem.
